text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- The Swiss Federal Railways board of directors approved a credit of 788 million Swiss francs for new tracks and improvements.

- Compagnie Financiere Richemont AG, a firm primarily dealing in tabacco, luxury goods and media, posted a 15 percent rise in sales to 2.34 billion pounds in the first six months of 1996 ended September 30.

- Switzerland struck a compromise in bilateral talks with the EU to start the free flow of people to and from EU countries after a transition period of 15 years. Switzerland has the possibility of backing out after 7 years.
- The Swiss government will decide tomorrow whether or not to provide a 130 million Swiss franc credit to the Expo 2001.
- Electro-engineering group ABB and Volvo Car Corporation are planning a joint venture in the automobile delivery industry.
- The Elektrizitaets Gesellschaft Laufenburg (EGL) increased its group results by 24.6 percent to 41 million Swiss francs in the 1995/96 fiscal year ending September 30.

- Geneva-based Republic National Bank of New York (Suisse) SA, controlled by the Edmond J. Safra Group, is taking over Mercury Bank in Zurich for some 250 million Swiss francs. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
